section_summary: This section concerns the publication and sale of Herbert O. Yardley’s The American Black Chamber and an unpublished manuscript about Japanese diplomatic messages. It includes correspondence with the publisher, the legislative history of the 1933 law protecting diplomatic codes, public criticism of the book’s suppression, and renewed requests to republish it in 1939. The final documents address confidential efforts to prevent imports of an English edition under copyright law.

people.name: William Phillips
people.role: Acting Secretary of State; later Under Secretary of State

people.name: D. L. Chambers
people.role: Vice President, later President, of The Bobbs-Merrill Company

people.name: Herbert O. Yardley
people.role: Author and former head of the American black chamber

people.name: South Trimble
people.role: Clerk of the House of Representatives

people.name: Joseph T. Robinson

people.name: Maxwell M. Hamilton
people.role: Assistant Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: Seihei Okuyama
people.role: Publisher, editor and printer of The Okuyama Service

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the publisher’s petition
subfiles.about: Advises limiting permission to sell The American Black Chamber to copies already printed.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth discusses the Attorney General’s referral of Bobbs-Merrill’s petition and recommends a direct State Department response, possibly allowing only sales of existing copies.

subfiles.title: Bobbs-Merrill request to print and distribute remaining contractual copies
subfiles.about: Requests assurance that the publisher may print and distribute the balance required by its contract.
subfiles.summary: Chambers cites contractual liability and mail order commitments and promises not to publicize the correspondence.

subfiles.title: State Department refusal to extend its assurance
subfiles.about: Declines to permit further printing of The American Black Chamber.
subfiles.summary: Phillips reaffirms the earlier assurance concerning copies printed before June 14, 1933, but says extending it to unprinted copies would conflict with the spirit of the June 10 law and United States interests.

subfiles.title: Caldwell’s protest over suppression of the book
subfiles.about: Protests the reported suppression of Yardley’s book.
subfiles.summary: Caldwell criticizes the government’s action and recalls his support for restoring the black chamber.

subfiles.title: Legislative history of H.R. 4220
subfiles.about: Provides the legislative history of the law protecting government records.
subfiles.summary: Lists the bill’s passage and approval dates and identifies the attached reports, bill and statute.

subfiles.title: House Judiciary Committee report on H.R. 4220
subfiles.about: Recommends a bill addressing unauthorized disclosure of government records and coded communications.
subfiles.summary: The report explains proposed amendments, argues for preventing leaks and damaging purported disclosures, and compares the House bill with existing criminal law.

subfiles.title: Senate Foreign Relations Committee report on H.R. 4220
subfiles.about: Recommends replacing the House text with a narrower diplomatic code provision.
subfiles.summary: The proposed amendment penalizes unauthorized publication or disclosure of diplomatic codes and intercepted diplomatic communications.

subfiles.title: Conference report and managers’ statement on H.R. 4220
subfiles.about: Recommends adoption of the Senate amendment.
subfiles.summary: The conference report accepts the Senate’s replacement text; the managers’ statement explains how it narrows the House bill to diplomatic codes and intercepted diplomatic matter.

subfiles.title: Act for the protection of government records
subfiles.about: Enacts penalties for unauthorized disclosure of diplomatic codes and certain diplomatic communications.
subfiles.summary: Public Law 37 sets fines and imprisonment for covered disclosures by persons with access through federal employment.

subfiles.title: Original H.R. 4220 and cover
subfiles.about: Introduces the original government records protection bill.
subfiles.summary: The visible bill text proposes penalties for federal employees who improperly conceal, alter, destroy or sell government material.

subfiles.title: Reply to Caldwell
subfiles.about: Directs Caldwell’s complaint about the book to Congress.
subfiles.summary: Moore sends the 1933 act and suggests seeking a legislative amendment.

subfiles.title: Alternative reply to Caldwell
subfiles.about: Offers an alternative explanation of the 1933 act.
subfiles.summary: The draft sends the act and says it primarily protects diplomatic codes.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser routing note
subfiles.about: Routes a question concerning the Caldwell correspondence.
subfiles.summary: A largely illegible handwritten note asks Vallance to consider the matter.

subfiles.title: Examination and Review routing note
subfiles.about: Records a brief internal handling note.
subfiles.summary: The handwritten note is largely illegible.

subfiles.title: Short reply to Caldwell
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Caldwell’s letter and encloses the government records act.
subfiles.summary: A short draft sends Caldwell a copy of the act.

subfiles.title: Tinkham letter quoting a press account of decoded Japanese messages
subfiles.about: Quotes a Boston Herald report of Yardley’s claims about intercepted Japanese messages.
subfiles.summary: The quoted report attributes United States negotiating advantages at the Washington Naval Conference to decoded Japanese messages.

subfiles.title: Receipt card handling note
subfiles.about: Notes where a signed receipt card was clipped.
subfiles.summary: Davenport identifies the receipt card’s location among the papers.

subfiles.title: Department of State delivery receipt
subfiles.about: Documents hand delivery of materials to the Attorney General.
subfiles.summary: A partly completed delivery form records the addressee and receipt fields.

subfiles.title: Note on returning Yardley’s manuscript
subfiles.about: Records a Justice Department request for a covering note when the manuscript is returned.
subfiles.summary: The note says State has no further interest in the manuscript and plans to transfer custody to Justice.

subfiles.title: Return of Japanese Diplomatic Secrets manuscript
subfiles.about: Returns Yardley’s unpublished manuscript to the Department of Justice.
subfiles.summary: Phillips recounts its acquisition through grand jury proceedings and transfers it for appropriate disposition.

subfiles.title: Justice Department receipt for Yardley manuscript
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the manuscript in seven parts.
subfiles.summary: Keenan confirms delivery of Japanese Diplomatic Secrets, 1921–1923.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs routing sheet
subfiles.about: Records internal circulation of an item.
subfiles.summary: The page contains only a division heading and brief routing marks.

subfiles.title: Japanese press digest on black chambers
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese Foreign Office plan to improve diplomatic code work.
subfiles.summary: The digest describes proposed specialist code officers at Japanese missions and efforts to devise stronger codes. A second item begins on page 164 about proposed baronies for Generals Araki and Honjō.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to report on Japanese code
subfiles.about: Points to another file concerning possession of a Japanese code and transcription difficulties.
subfiles.summary: The note cross-references file 821.6363/1284.

subfiles.title: Note on misrouted papers
subfiles.about: Explains that papers were sidetracked in the European Affairs division.
subfiles.summary: Hickerson apologizes and offers to discuss or file the papers.

subfiles.title: Gigax inquiry about codebreaking and naval conferences
subfiles.about: Asks whether the government still conducts work like that described by Yardley.
subfiles.summary: Gigax cites Yardley’s account of the Washington and London naval conferences and requests a private answer.

subfiles.title: Reply to Gigax
subfiles.about: Declines detailed discussion and disputes Yardley’s explanation of conference outcomes.
subfiles.summary: Moffat says the Washington and London conference results should not be attributed to the presence or absence of the information Gigax described.

subfiles.title: Earlier draft reply to Gigax
subfiles.about: Proposes a fuller rejection of Yardley’s account of the conferences.
subfiles.summary: The draft stresses the participating governments’ interests and urges caution about claims linking conference success or failure to intercepted information.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser memorandum on a reply to Gigax
subfiles.about: Offers draft language for answering Gigax’s letter.
subfiles.summary: Ward found no suitable precedent. His draft disputes the claim that access to intercepted information determined naval conference outcomes and questions the source’s self-interested assessment.

subfiles.title: Senator Van Nuys’s referral of Bobbs-Merrill request
subfiles.about: Asks the State Department to consider Bobbs-Merrill’s request favorably.
subfiles.summary: Van Nuys forwards the publisher’s letter and requests assistance.

subfiles.title: Bobbs-Merrill request to resume publication
subfiles.about: Seeks clearance to publish a new American edition of The American Black Chamber.
subfiles.summary: Chambers recounts the 1933 restriction, argues that circumstances have changed, and says imported English copies are being sold while the American edition remains unavailable.

subfiles.title: Messersmith request for advice
subfiles.about: Requests a review of the publisher’s case and advice for replying to Van Nuys.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith forwards Van Nuys’s letter and its enclosure for examination.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser note on the senator’s letter
subfiles.about: Notes handling of a proposed reply to Van Nuys.
subfiles.summary: The handwritten direction is largely illegible.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs opinion on republication
subfiles.about: Advises against republication because it could renew Japanese resentment.
subfiles.summary: The division considers republication inadvisable even if legally possible.

subfiles.title: Hackworth referral to Hornbeck
subfiles.about: Assigns the draft reply to Van Nuys to Hornbeck.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth cites Hornbeck’s earlier work on the book and its connection to Japan.

subfiles.title: Interim acknowledgment to Van Nuys
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the publisher’s request and promises review.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith says the Department will examine the matter and respond.

subfiles.title: Letter to Postmaster General about English edition imports
subfiles.about: Alerts postal authorities to reported imports of an English edition.
subfiles.summary: Hull sends the Chambers correspondence, invokes copyright import authority, and asks that any action receive little publicity.

subfiles.title: Letter to Treasury Secretary about English edition imports
subfiles.about: Alerts customs authorities to reported imports of an English edition.
subfiles.summary: Hull forwards the correspondence, points to Treasury’s copyright import authority, and asks for minimal publicity.

subfiles.title: Final reply to Van Nuys
subfiles.about: Declines to change the Department’s 1933 position on republication.
subfiles.summary: Hull encloses the 1933 correspondence, says he has nothing to add, and reports that postal and Treasury officials have been informed about English edition imports.

subfiles.title: Postmaster General’s acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Reports instructions to watch for English editions in incoming mail.
subfiles.summary: Receiving post offices are told to prevent unlawful delivery and avoid publicity.

subfiles.title: Treasury reply on foreign editions
subfiles.about: Reports confidential customs instructions against importation of foreign editions.
subfiles.summary: Treasury cites the American copyright and says customs officers will receive a confidential vigilance circular.

subfiles.title: Confidential Bureau of Customs circular
subfiles.to: Collectors of Customs and other officers
subfiles.about: Orders vigilance against imported foreign editions of The American Black Chamber.
subfiles.summary: The circular invokes copyright law and directs officers to treat the matter confidentially.

subfiles.title: Draft Treasury reply
subfiles.about: Drafts Treasury’s acknowledgment and account of customs action.
subfiles.summary: The draft describes the copyright registration and confidential circular.

subfiles.title: Second draft Treasury reply
subfiles.about: Repeats Treasury’s proposed response concerning imported English copies.
subfiles.summary: The draft says customs officers will prevent imports and keep the matter confidential.

subfiles.title: Record of consultation on confidential customs circular
subfiles.about: Records discussions about the unpublished Yardley book and the customs circular.
subfiles.summary: Clendenin asks whether Yardley’s second book appeared and whether a confidential circular is suitable. Salisbury says the manuscript was not published and confirms that the circular should direct customs officers to keep action on The American Black Chamber confidential.
